question: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a continuous function. Suppose $$f(x)=\frac{1}{t}\int_0^t\bigl(f(x+y)-f(y)\bigr)\,dy$$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$ and all $t>0$. Then show that there exists a constant $c$ such that $f(x)=cx$ for all $x$.

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10 + 2 Level
